title: Opening: names, address and date of the interview
summary: White gives his name and home; Allen records the date, March 3, 1961, and introduces the participants. White does not know his birth date and mentions wanting a job.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: My name is Horace White. H-O-R-A-C-E. W-H-I-T-E. That's my name, Horace White.
Let's see, and we're recording this today. This is your home where you live, huh?
Yes sir. This is my home where I live, right here. And that's my aunt. The one in the back, and that's my cousin right there. That's my cousin right there, sitting on there.
Maybe we can get him to get you an ashtray. I think he's in front of me.
Right here? No, you might not be able to reach that.
Yeah, I didn't want to. Yeah, I didn't want to mess the place up. Anyhow, let's see. It says 1842 Paulger Street.
Yes sir. Old Bourbon, huh? Old Bourbon Street.
And let's see, what's today's date? It's March.
March the 3rd.
March the 3rd of 1961. That's right. Okay, well we'll just, I'd like to get the date of your birth too, if we can.
Now, that's something I don't know because my people never did sit down and told me how old I was, you understand? And my people would sit down like y'all would. You understand what I mean?
And the time he was born, they didn't have all that you have now, like braces, you know all that. Oh yeah. But he's old enough because he's on all age with you.

You see, I didn't know my age. But, I was about, but I gave myself about 17 years old when I was, used to be second line. And I was second, and I was second line, I was second line all through you, all uptown, all through the district, all up, all up in Carlton. Wasn't a place you can call. I didn't know nothing about. But here now, I didn't say, you know what I mean? I don't mean, I don't mean in the country nowhere else, or outside, outside of New Orleans. Now, I would like, if I couldn't get me a place to be in a, you know, get me, get me a little job with some northern people, I'd be glad to get me a little job. If it wouldn't be doing nothing but sweeping, or, you know, or be a wife in the shop. Because plenty of times, plenty of times I have to wait, I have to wait so long for a little bit,
you understand? Oh yeah, you're on your old age pension plan.
Yes. But you got to wait so long before you get it, you see. So like that, I'd rather be working, you understand? Like that, I would like to be working, and have, have what I want.
Can we get your niece's name on here since you talk?
Mine? Dorothy Harris.
See, Dorothy Harris. And, uh, I'm Dick Allen. Let's get your name on here.
Oh, Marjorie Zander.
See, the secretary up, up at school, where, at Tulane, you know.
Oh, Tulane, Tulane, Tulane, that's what you see?
Yeah, that's where we work, you know. She types all this up, and I want her to get everybody's name down straight, so she can, you know, notice on the tape when she hears it.
No.
